page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.large is a general-purpose instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a burstable CPU model powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor clocked at 3.2 GHz across an x86_64 architecture. Hardware resources consist of a single physical core mapped to two vCPUs via hyper-threading, accompanied by 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 105 MB L3 cache pool. System memory totals 8.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 5 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local instance storage or GPU acceleration.

Benchmark testing highlights solid single-threaded performance contrasted with lower aggregate parallel capacity. Single-core evaluations place the instance in the middle tier, achieving 1607.88 in stress-ng single-core tests and 1742.0 in Geekbench single-core assessments. Instruction set accelerators including AVX-512 and Intel AMX facilitate specialized mathematical routines. Conversely, constrained thread concurrency limits multi-threaded throughput, producing a multi-core Geekbench score of 2210.0 and a multi-core stress-ng result of 1899.38. Uncached large-block memory read throughput is measured at 12.74 GB/sec alongside write throughput of 14.08 GB/sec, reflecting entry-level memory sub-system results in PassMark memory testing.

The burstable delivery model provides qualitative cost advantages for applications that operate with low baseline CPU utilization and require periodic burst capacity. Because persistent execution at maximum utilization is restricted by the burstable allocation model, the instance is ill-suited for sustained compute-intensive batch processing, high-throughput caching, or large relational database backends. Measured Redis throughput reaches 2.43 million operations per second, and static web serving achieves 4.0 GB/sec. Consequently, the m7i-flex.large represents a practical configuration for lightweight web servers, API microservices, continuous integration runners, staging environments, and entry-tier monitoring agents.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.large is a general-purpose virtual machine utilizing a burstable CPU allocation profile on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8488C x86_64 processor offering one physical core and two vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz, delivering a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, while containing zero local storage and no GPU accelerators. In synthetic benchmarks, single-threaded metrics reflect average performance, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1742.0 and stress-ng single-core rating of 1607.88. However, multi-core and memory throughput fall into the lower tiers due to the constrained two-vCPU baseline, with multi-core Geekbench reaching 2210.0 and PassMark memory scoring 948.41. The burstable baseline provides qualitative cost savings for workloads with intermittent CPU activity. The instance is primarily appropriate for entry-level web serving, dev-test environments, lightweight background workers, and microservices.
